original_statement:
What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. The Core accepts an edit that removes the head site's error and exposes any number of later errors in the same declaration. A site position is the pair (declaration index in source order, bytes from the error to the end of that declaration). The Core sorts open sites by that position. A D12 statement follow and its body edit are one candidate. Decisions X1 to X8 and the S1 acceptance check of docs/parallel.md hold.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. LeanMend/Core/Mend.lean accepts an edit when the module error count falls, or when the count is unchanged and Candidate.exposes finds exactly one new site. An edit that exposes two later errors is rejected. The open sites are in Lean's message order: in EVMLean run 20, Semantics site 1040 was the head site while site 288 was open. In EVMLean run 20, a valCompare edit at Semantics 1040 lowered the error count from 5 to 4, and the Core rejected it. That build measured the byte distance to the end of the file, and the distance of site 288 grew by the bytes that the edit added.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run scripts/gate.sh. Run the fixtures tests/fixtures/expose-two and tests/fixtures/expose-back through tests/expose.sh, as docs/parallel.md S1 states. Run lean-mend on EVMLean and read the Semantics entries in mend-target/.lean-mend/ledger.jsonl: the valCompare attempt at line 1040 is accepted. The EVMLean target is ~/code/git_puller/repos/EVMLean/.scratch/mend-target, a git worktree of ~/code/git_puller/repos/EVMLean on branch lean-mend-adopt. Before a run, reset it with: git switch -q lean-mend-adopt; git branch -D lean-mend/mend; rm -rf .lean-mend; git worktree prune. Do not remove any other worktree of the EVMLean repository: .scratch/conf holds conformance results. The run command, from ~/code/git_puller/repos/EVMLean/.scratch, with PATH including .scratch/pyenv/bin and ~/.elan/bin: <lean-mend binary> run mend-target --adopt --prepare "lake exe cache get" --annotate-binders --follow-definition-changes --rules <lean-mend>/rules/proposed. One sequential run takes about 2 hours. Only one EVMLean run may use the host at a time: one large lean process uses about 2.2 GiB, and swap is 0.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. Spec and Core import no Shell module (scripts/gate.sh checks it). Termination stays a theorem in LeanMend/Spec/Termination.lean, with no retry cap and no timeout as a control. Decision D10 holds: lean-mend adds no declaration to a target. lean-mend depends on Lean core only, not on Mathlib. Every committed text is in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Run export PATH="$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH" before a lean or lake command. Scratch files go in the gitignored .scratch/ directory, not /tmp.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) LeanMend/Core/Mend.lean, LeanMend/Core/Ops.lean, LeanMend/Spec/Types.lean, LeanMend/Spec/Termination.lean, LeanMend/Spec/Invariant.lean, LeanMend/Shell/Target.lean, LeanMend/Shell/Driver.lean, probe/Probe.lean regions
restatement: The lean-mend Core must judge an edit by the source position of the earliest open error. It must not judge by the module error count or by the count of newly exposed sites. A site position is the pair (declaration index in source order, bytes from the error to the end of that declaration). The Core sorts open sites by that position, so the head site is the earliest error, not the first error in Lean's message order. The Core accepts an edit that removes the head site's error and exposes any number of later errors in the same declaration. The Core rejects an edit that leaves or adds an error earlier than the old head. A D12 statement follow and its body edit are one candidate, so the earliest error never moves back. Decisions X1 to X8 and the S1 acceptance check of docs/parallel.md hold. The existing limits stay. Spec and Core import no Shell module. Termination stays a theorem in LeanMend/Spec/Termination.lean, with no retry cap and no timeout as a control. The measure uses Lean core Prod.Lex only and is not a multiset order. lean-mend does not depend on Mathlib. This repairs the EVMLean run 20 failure, where a valCompare edit at Semantics 1040 lowered the error count from 5 to 4 and the Core rejected it.

goal: The Core accepts an edit that exposes several later errors in the same declaration, orders sites by (declaration index, bytes to declaration end), and rejects an edit that exposes an earlier error.
acceptance_criteria: The expose-two example is an edit that fixes the first error and reveals two later errors in the same declaration. The tool reports that it accepts the edit.
The expose-back example is an edit that reveals an error before the old first error. The tool reports that it rejects the edit.
In the order-first example, Lean lists a later error first, and an earlier error sits before it in the source. The tool reports that it picked the source-earliest error as the head.
In the follow-pair example, a statement follow and its body edit are applied together. The tool reports one judged candidate, and it accepts that candidate.
The project gate script runs and prints its result as one JSON object. The result field says every check passed.
The design document still carries all eight decisions X1 to X8.
No Spec or Core source file imports a Shell module.
The termination file still states termination as a theorem.
No Spec or Core file uses a retry cap or a timeout as a control.
The termination file builds its measure from Prod.Lex.
No Spec or Core file imports Mathlib or uses a multiset order.
